basics.name: Yiyang Huang
basics.summary: I am a Ph.D. candidate in Computer Engineering at Northeastern University. I study how multimodal agents use tools and learn from feedback, how vision-language models understand long videos, and why they hallucinate.

education.area: B.Eng. in Intelligence Science and Technology

work.summary: Advised by Prof. Yun Raymond Fu.
highlights: Developed RACER, a training-free agent that decomposes questions, retrieves video frames, and refines its search using visual feedback. Across four video LLMs, it improved accuracy over uniform sampling by 4.3–6.6 percentage points on Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench.

Developed SHIELD to address encoder bias with inference-time token interventions and adversarial contrastive decoding. It reduced captioning hallucinations by 27% relative to the baseline across multiple vision-language model families.

Developed D-CoDe to adapt image-pretrained models to video question answering through question decomposition and dynamic frame and token compression. It improved accuracy on egocentric videos by 29% relative to the LLaVA-NeXT-7B baseline.

work.summary: Studied multimodal agents, VLM reasoning, and self-improvement with mentors Zhaowen Wang and Shraman Pramanick.
highlights: Built DesignJudge, a dataset of 7,475 layout preference pairs. Post-trained Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.8-27B to critique and score layouts.
Developed a loop in which a VLM evaluator critiques a layout, a Codex agent edits it, and the evaluator scores the result. Used the resulting preference pairs for iterative GRPO training.
GRACE-27B reached 83.7% accuracy on DesignJudge. In a user study, a majority of raters preferred GRACE-guided edits to Gemini-guided edits on 70% of the Crello layouts.

work.summary: Mentored by Zhaowen Wang, Simon Jenni, and Jing Shi.
highlights: Developed MASON to ground layout metadata in the image and model the 3D structure of design elements. With Qwen2.5-VL-7B as its backbone, MASON achieved relative improvements of 26% over Gemini-2.5-Pro and 15% over GPT-5/GPT-o3.
Built CoDeLayout, a benchmark of approximately 20,000 examples, by mining compositional structure and generating multimodal questions and answers.
